disclaimer: Educational decision support only. Similar symptoms can have non-disease causes. Confirm diagnosis with a KVK, agricultural extension officer, or plant pathologist. Use only products registered for the crop and disease locally and follow the current label.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown margins
Neck infection causes white or empty panicles
prevention: Use resistant varieties and healthy seed
Avoid excess nitrogen and prolonged leaf wetness
treatment: Use a registered blast fungicide only according to local thresholds
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Water-soaked streaks start at leaf tips and margins
Seedlings may wilt; lesions become yellow then straw coloured
prevention: Use resistant varieties and clean seed
Avoid excess nitrogen, leaf injury, and contaminated irrigation
treatment: Drain excess water and avoid spreading bacteria
Bactericides are often unreliable; obtain local diagnostic advice
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Round to oval brown spots with grey centres on leaves
Grain may show dark discoloration and poor filling
prevention: Correct potassium or other nutrient stress and manage residue
treatment: Improve crop nutrition and water management
Use registered seed or foliar treatment only after diagnosis
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Oval green-grey lesions on sheaths near the waterline
Lesions enlarge upward and may lodge plants
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen and dense planting
Manage weeds, infected residue, and water level
treatment: Use a registered sheath-blight product based on local risk advice
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Individual grains become velvety yellow-orange balls
Balls later turn greenish-black and may contaminate seed
prevention: Use clean seed and balanced fertilizer
Remove infected panicles and residue; avoid excess nitrogen
treatment: Collect and destroy smut balls before they burst
Discuss locally timed preventive fungicide options before heading
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Oblong brown lesions occur on the flag-leaf sheath
Panicles emerge poorly and grains may be sterile or discoloured
prevention: Use healthy seed and resistant varieties
Control insects that injure sheaths and avoid excess nitrogen
treatment: Seek locally registered seed and foliar management advice
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails
